intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The naturally heated water sits at a perfect 37–39°C year-round. Includes access to steam caves, a lava sauna, and in-water silica mud mask treatments for a full rejuvenating experience.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling hot springs, and a small geyser. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this offers an authentic and intimate geothermal bathing experience in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Icelandic Food & Culture Walking Tour in Reykjavík
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavík's vibrant food scene on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and the infamous hákarl (fermented shark). Visit local markets and learn about Viking-era culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified guide, then descend into a breathtaking natural ice cave glowing in shades of blue and crystal. Learn about Iceland's glacial geology and climate change impacts while experiencing one of the country's most dramatic landscapes up close.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and baggage claim, then take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK) or shared airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront room, and get a good night's rest. If the sky is clear, step outside briefly to scan for northern lights — January nights in Iceland offer excellent aurora opportunities even from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at Keflavík Airport (Subway or airport café) before or after landing to keep costs low (~1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Download the Veðurstofa (Icelandic Met Office) app for real-time northern lights forecasts. Keep your curtains open or set a late-night alarm for aurora alerts. Exchange some currency or use a no-fee travel card for local purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, explore the immediate beachfront area around the resort. Walk along the black sand shoreline, breathe the crisp Arctic air, and take in dramatic coastal views. January sunrise is around 11:00 AM, so enjoy the golden-hour light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Blue Lagoon area (exterior views are free; entry tickets ~7,000–9,000 ISK if budget allows, or save for a cheaper hot spring later). Alternatively, drive or take a local bus to Grindavík town for a free stroll around the fishing harbor and to stock up on groceries at Krónan or Bónus supermarket for budget snacks and meals.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. After dark (around 16:00–17:00), bundle up and position yourself on the beach for northern lights watching. The beachfront location with minimal light pollution is ideal. Check aurora forecast app — if KP index is 3+, chances are good.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort or nearby bakery — skyr, bread, and coffee (~800 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed supermarket lunch — sandwich, fruit, and juice (~1,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Bónus, or try Grindavík's Bryggjan Café for affordable fish soup (~2,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on groceries today — this will save significant money throughout the trip. Buy instant oatmeal, skyr, bread, deli meats, and snacks. Bónus is Iceland's most budget-friendly supermarket chain.

day_by_day.morning: Head out to the Reykjanes Peninsula for a self-guided lava field walk. The Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark is free to enter. Walk the trails around Krýsuvík geothermal area, where you'll see bubbling mud pools, steaming fumaroles, and vivid sulfur-colored earth — completely free of charge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Seltún Geothermal Area (free entry), a colorful hot spring and mud pot field with well-marked boardwalk trails. Then drive to Kleifarvatn, Iceland's largest lake on the Reykjanes Peninsula, for eerie, moody winter landscape photography. The volcanic scenery is otherworldly.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort as darkness falls. Stop at Reykjanes Lighthouse (Reykjanesviti), Iceland's oldest lighthouse, for dramatic coastal views. After dark, set up for northern lights observation on the peninsula — the dark skies here are excellent. Return to resort for a warm dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort — oatmeal with skyr and fruit (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch from supermarket supplies (~800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hot meal at resort — pasta with canned tomato sauce and cheese (~600 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Wear waterproof, windproof layers and sturdy hiking boots. January temperatures hover around -2°C to 4°C but wind chill can be severe on the peninsula. Daylight is limited to about 5–6 hours, so plan outdoor activities between 11:00 and 16:00.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Reykjavík (45-minute drive or Strætó bus from Grindavík area, ~1,800 ISK one way). Start at Hallgrímskirkja church — exterior is free, tower elevator costs ~1,000 ISK. Walk down Skólavörðustígur street browsing local shops without buying.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Reykjavík waterfront (Harpa Concert Hall exterior, Rainbow Street, Old Harbour). Visit the Reykjavík Flea Market (Kolaportið) if it's a weekend — entry is free and you can find cheap Icelandic snacks and woolens. Walk through the city center and enjoy street art.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the Strætó bus back toward the resort before the last bus of the evening. On the return journey or from the resort, watch for northern lights. The bus ride itself through dark countryside can offer aurora sightings through the windows.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's famous hot dog stand in Reykjavík, a budget icon (~600 ISK for a hot dog with everything)
meals.dinner: Hlölla Bátar submarine sandwich shop in Reykjavík (~1,800 ISK) or self-catered back at resort

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjavík City Card is not worth it for a single day on a tight budget. Stick to free attractions. Download the Strætó app for real-time bus schedules. Many Reykjavík museums have free entry on specific days — check schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning and aurora recovery day if you had a late night watching lights. Late breakfast, then visit the Gunnuhver Hot Springs on the Reykjanes Peninsula — a powerful geothermal area with dramatic steam vents and boiling mud pools. Free to visit, just a short drive from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bridge Between Continents (Miðlína) — a small footbridge spanning the rift between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Entry is free (certificate purchase is optional at ~1,500 ISK). Walk along the rift valley and marvel at this geological wonder.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a relaxing evening. Prepare a warm soup or stew from supermarket ingredients. Set a midnight alarm and check aurora forecast — clear January nights with high KP index are prime aurora viewing time from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs, toast, and skyr (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Thermos of hot soup and packed sandwiches eaten near Gunnuhver (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered lamb soup using pre-made soup mix from Bónus (~900 ISK for a large pot)

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver is one of Iceland's most powerful geothermal areas — stay on marked paths and behind barriers. The steam and sulfur smell are intense. This is a completely free, spectacular alternative to paid hot spring experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or arrange a budget car rental for the Golden Circle (can be done as a self-drive day trip). First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — free entry, UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk the rift valley, see Öxará River, and explore Iceland's ancient parliament site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Geysir Geothermal Area — free to walk around and watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes. Then drive to Gullfoss Waterfall — free entry, one of Iceland's most iconic waterfalls, dramatic even in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort (about 1.5–2 hours). Stop at Kerið volcanic crater if time allows (~400 ISK entry fee). Watch for northern lights on the rural drive back — pull over safely in dark areas for the best views.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed thermos lunch eaten at Geysir parking area (~800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered or stop at a Reykjavík N1 gas station for a budget hot dog and soup (~1,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Renting a small car for this day costs approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK including fuel. Split with other travelers if possible. Alternatively, budget Golden Circle bus tours start around 8,000–10,000 ISK. Roads may be icy — drive carefully and check road.is for conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and do laundry if needed. Spend the morning journaling, reviewing photos, and planning the second half of the trip. Walk the beachfront for fresh air and coastal views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Svartsengi geothermal power plant area (exterior views free) and explore the surrounding lava fields on foot. The landscape around the resort area is hauntingly beautiful — moss-covered lava, steam rising from vents, and dramatic skies.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights evening. Check the aurora forecast carefully. If KP index is 3 or above and skies are clear, drive away from any light sources to a dark spot on the peninsula. Bring a tripod for long-exposure photography. Stay out for 1–2 hours scanning the sky.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered big breakfast — eggs, toast, skyr, fruit (~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Self-catered — leftovers and fresh bread from supermarket (~500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself slightly — try Salthúsið restaurant in Grindavík for fresh fish of the day (~3,500–4,500 ISK) or self-cater for ~800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to restock groceries at Bónus or Krónan. Also check weather forecasts for the coming days to plan excursions strategically around clear nights for aurora viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Eldvörp lava shield and volcanic craters on the Reykjanes Peninsula — completely free hiking area with dramatic volcanic scenery. The trail is relatively flat and accessible even in winter with proper footwear. Bring hiking poles for icy patches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Strandarkirkja, the famous 'Sailors' Church' on the southern Reykjanes coast — a tiny, beautiful historic church on the shoreline. Free to visit. Continue along the southern coast road for scenic winter seascape views and birdwatching (winter seabirds).
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Warm up with a hot drink and prepare dinner. If aurora forecast is favorable, head back out after 21:00 for northern lights viewing from the dark beachfront. The coastal location can offer reflections of the aurora on the water on calm nights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — oatmeal with honey and dried fruit (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Thermos of hot chocolate and packed sandwiches on the trail (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta carbonara (~700 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January hiking requires microspikes or crampons for icy trails — available to rent or buy cheaply at Bónus or outdoor shops. Always tell someone your hiking plan and check weather before heading out on trails.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward Selfoss and the south coast. Visit Urriðafoss waterfall (free, Iceland's highest-volume waterfall by water flow) and Þjórsárdalur valley for scenic winter landscapes. The drive along Route 1 offers stunning mountain and valley views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Skálholt Cathedral (free entry) — one of Iceland's most historically significant sites, Iceland's former episcopal seat. Then explore Flúðir village, known for its geothermal activity. The Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir is Iceland's oldest swimming pool and more affordable than Blue Lagoon (~3,000 ISK entry).
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the Secret Lagoon as darkness falls — the combination of warm geothermal water and potential northern lights overhead is magical and budget-friendly. Drive back to resort afterward.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten near Urriðafoss (~800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered warm dinner upon return to resort (~700 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is one of the best budget hot spring alternatives in Iceland. It's natural, uncrowded compared to Blue Lagoon, and the setting is authentic. Book online in advance. Total driving for this day is approximately 3–4 hours round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Reykjavík's free museums and cultural sites. The Settlement Exhibition (871±2) costs ~2,000 ISK but is worth it, or visit the National Museum of Iceland (~2,000 ISK) for deep Icelandic history. Alternatively, the Reykjavík Art Museum has rotating free days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavík's Laugardalur area — free outdoor spaces, the Laugardalur botanical garden (free in winter), and Laugardalslaug public swimming pool (~1,100 ISK entry). Icelanders' beloved geothermal public pools are a budget-friendly hot spring experience — socialize with locals in hot tubs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's evening atmosphere on a budget — walk Laugavegur street, window shop, and enjoy the city lights. Head back to resort. If it's a clear night, the drive back through dark countryside is prime aurora territory.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at resort (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Reykjavík Roasters coffee shop for coffee and pastry (~1,200 ISK), or Sandholt Bakery for fresh bread and soup (~1,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Noodle Station in Reykjavík — budget-friendly Asian noodle soup, very popular (~1,800–2,200 ISK) or self-catered at resort

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug public pool is a quintessential Icelandic experience. The hot tubs (heitur pottur) are where locals gather and chat — a genuine cultural experience for just ~1,100 ISK. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees.

day_by_day.morning: Northern lights recovery morning if you had a successful late-night sighting. After a late breakfast, explore the Grindavík area on foot — the town's harbor, the Kvikan House of Culture and Natural Resources (small local museum, ~500 ISK), and the local fishing culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Þórbergssetur in Hali (or explore closer Reykjanes sites) — alternatively, spend the afternoon at Kleifarvatn lake for a peaceful winter walk along the frozen or semi-frozen shoreline. The lake's desolate beauty is extraordinary in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated aurora hunting evening. Choose the darkest available location — ideally away from resort lights, facing north. Bring hot drinks in a thermos, warm blankets, and patience. January in Iceland statistically offers some of the best aurora viewing of the year.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered big brunch (~600 ISK)
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch (~700 ISK)
meals.dinner: Celebrate potential aurora success with a slightly special dinner — try Grindavík's local restaurant or a step-up self-catered meal with lamb chops from Bónus (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: For the best aurora photography, use manual mode on your camera: ISO 1600–3200, aperture f/2.8 or wider, shutter speed 10–25 seconds. A smartphone with a night mode can also capture decent aurora images. The aurora app 'My Aurora Forecast' is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit your favorite spot from the trip for a last look. Consider a final morning walk along the beachfront at sunrise (~11:00 AM) to absorb the atmosphere. Pack non-essentials and begin organizing luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping on a budget — Bónus supermarket sells affordable Icelandic chocolates, licorice, and skyr products as gifts. Avoid tourist shops in Reykjavík for souvenirs as they're expensive. Alternatively, a final drive around the Reykjanes Peninsula for a farewell to the volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt from the resort beachfront. Even if clouds obscure the sky, enjoy the sound of the ocean and the crisp Arctic air. Prepare a special self-catered farewell dinner using remaining groceries. Review the trip, organize receipts, and relax.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — use up remaining breakfast supplies (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Final Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog in Reykjavík if passing through, or self-catered (~600–800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell self-catered dinner — use remaining groceries creatively, perhaps a skyr dessert with berries (~800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Check out procedures with the resort for your departure day. Confirm your airport transfer or Flybus booking for tomorrow. The Flybus must be booked to correspond with your flight — book online at re.is for best prices (~3,000 ISK). Duty-free at Keflavík airport is excellent for last-minute Icelandic spirits and chocolate.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on your departure flight time, you may have time for one last geothermal area visit or a final drive through the lava fields. Take the Flybus or arranged transfer to Keflavík International Airport (allow 45–60 minutes travel time plus check-in time).
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure procedures — check in, security, and explore duty-free shopping at Keflavík. The airport has good food options and free WiFi. Browse Icelandic woolens, spirits, and chocolate at duty-free for final gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with memories of geothermal wonders, volcanic landscapes, and hopefully dazzling northern lights. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring Iceland on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at resort using last supplies (~400 ISK) or grab something at the airport
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snacks from remaining supplies (~1,000–1,500 ISK at airport)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days: Accommodation (resort), groceries ~25,000 ISK, transport ~15,000 ISK, activities ~12,000 ISK, dining out ~18,000 ISK — total out-of-pocket approximately 70,000–85,000 ISK (~500–600 USD) excluding accommodation. Self-catering is the single biggest money-saver in Iceland.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer or rental car to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront room, and unwind with a warm drink from the hotel bar. Peek outside – January skies can already reveal the Northern Lights on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Light snack at the airport or hotel bar upon arrival – try a bowl of Icelandic lamb soup if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night very light. Confirm your rental car or transfer in advance. Pack layers in your carry-on as Iceland in January averages -1°C to 3°C. January offers up to 19 hours of potential Northern Lights viewing windows each night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast with views of the Icelandic coastline. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront near the resort to breathe in the crisp Arctic air and get your bearings. Sunrise in January is around 11:00 AM, so there is no rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a short transfer to the famous Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (approximately 20–30 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula area). Soak in Iceland's iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy the in-water bar, silica mud mask treatment, and the surreal steaming landscape. Book the Comfort Package for a mid-range experience including towel and one drink.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out for dinner in a nearby town or the hotel restaurant. Afterward, check the Aurora Forecast app – if activity is rated 3 or above and skies are clear, step outside your beachfront room for a spontaneous Northern Lights viewing from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – eggs, skyr, smoked salmon, and Icelandic bread
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant (mid-range option) – try the langoustine soup or Icelandic fish of the day
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near the resort or hotel dining – grilled Arctic char with roasted root vegetables and a glass of Icelandic craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Blue Lagoon tickets well in advance – they sell out weeks ahead. Bring a hair tie as the silica can tangle hair. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes for easy changing. January sunset is around 4:30 PM so afternoon light is brief and beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, drive toward Reykjavík (approximately 40–50 minutes from the Reykjanes area). Begin exploring Iceland's capital on foot. Visit Hallgrímskirkja Church for panoramic city views from the tower, then stroll down Skólavörðustígur street browsing local design shops and galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Icelandic Food & Culture Walking Tour in Reykjavík. Explore the city's vibrant food scene with a knowledgeable guide through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb, rye bread, dried fish, and Brennivín schnapps. Learn about Viking heritage and modern Icelandic culture as you walk through colorful streets.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's lively downtown area around Laugavegur street. Browse bookshops, pop into a cozy café, and enjoy the charming winter atmosphere. Drive back to the resort. Before bed, check aurora forecasts and step outside if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the Food & Culture Walking Tour – supplement with a bowl of lamb soup at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (mid-range) or Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) for grilled langoustine skewers on a budget – a beloved Reykjavík institution

day_by_day.notes: Wear very comfortable walking shoes. The food tour typically lasts 3–4 hours. Book the tour in advance. Parking in Reykjavík city center requires paid meters on weekdays – Sunday is often free. Daylight hours are limited so make the most of midday light for sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from the resort toward the famous Golden Circle route. First stop: Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley and learn about the world's oldest parliament established here in 930 AD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then drive to the magnificent Gullfoss waterfall – even in winter the partially frozen falls are breathtaking. Pack crampons or rent them locally for icy paths.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the resort. If skies are clear and aurora activity is forecast, pull over in a dark rural area away from light pollution for Northern Lights viewing from the car. Arrive back at the resort for a warm dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – pack snacks and a thermos of coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Geysir Center cafeteria or Friðheimar greenhouse restaurant (famous for tomato soup and fresh tomatoes grown with geothermal energy – book ahead)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort or a nearby grill – try Icelandic lamb stew (kjötsúpa)

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle loop is approximately 300 km and takes a full day. Roads in January can be icy – check road.is before departing. Drive slowly and safely. Dress in waterproof layers as Gullfoss spray can be intense even in winter. Sunset around 4:30 PM so plan Gullfoss visit before then for best light.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at the resort. After a late breakfast, visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir – Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Soak in the natural hot spring pool surrounded by a steaming landscape, small geysers, and complete tranquility. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and wonderfully authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Secret Lagoon, explore the charming village of Flúðir and its surrounding farmland. Drive back toward the resort via scenic Route 1. Stop at any roadside viewpoints or waterfalls that catch your eye – Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss are reachable as a detour if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for dinner. Spend the evening in the hotel lounge or on the beachfront watching for Northern Lights. January is peak aurora season with long dark nights offering excellent viewing opportunities.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the hotel or grab a sandwich from a local bakery near Flúðir – try Icelandic kleinur (twisted doughnuts) from a local shop
meals.dinner: Hotel dining – opt for pan-seared cod with butter sauce and Icelandic potatoes, paired with a local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon tickets should be booked online in advance. Water temperature is a constant 38–40°C – perfect for cold January days. Bring a towel and swimsuit. The drive from the resort to Flúðir is approximately 1.5–2 hours depending on your base location.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and begin the scenic drive east along the South Coast – one of Iceland's most dramatic stretches of road. Stop at Seljalandsfoss waterfall (you can walk behind it – bring waterproofs) and Skógafoss waterfall for stunning photos in the winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach near Vík – a hauntingly beautiful volcanic beach with towering basalt columns and dramatic sea stacks called Reynisdrangar. Observe the powerful Atlantic waves from a safe distance (these waves are extremely dangerous – never turn your back on the ocean). Visit the charming village of Vík for a hot drink.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in Vík or nearby for the night. After dinner, join a Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour departing from the Vík area. A small-group guided jeep tour takes you away from light pollution into the Icelandic wilderness for the best possible aurora viewing conditions with expert guidance.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before checkout
meals.lunch: Skógar Museum café near Skógafoss or a packed lunch from a roadside stop – try a hot dog from a local petrol station (an Icelandic tradition)
meals.dinner: Halldórskaffi restaurant in Vík – cozy atmosphere with hearty Icelandic lamb and fish dishes at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel-heavy day covering approximately 180–200 km. Check road.is for conditions. Book the Northern Lights Jeep tour in advance as small-group tours fill quickly. The tour operator will advise on the best departure time based on aurora forecasts. Wear your warmest layers for the night tour.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-earned rest following last night's aurora hunt, enjoy breakfast at your Vík accommodation. Drive east to explore the Eldhraun lava field – a vast moss-covered lava plain from the 1783 Laki eruption. Continue to Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon, a stunning 100-meter deep canyon carved by glacial meltwater (check access as it may be restricted in winter).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving east toward the Glacier Lagoon area. Stop at Kirkjubæjarklaustur village for lunch and fuel. Arrive at Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon in the late afternoon – witness enormous icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier floating serenely in the lagoon. Visit adjacent Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Check into accommodation near Jökulsárlón or in the Höfn area. Enjoy dinner featuring Höfn's legendary langoustine – this small fishing town is the langoustine capital of Iceland. Keep eyes on the sky for Northern Lights reflecting in the glacier lagoon for a truly magical experience.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Vík
meals.lunch: Systrakaffi café in Kirkjubæjarklaustur – home-cooked Icelandic meals including lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Pakkhús Restaurant in Höfn – famous for langoustine dishes at mid-range prices; try the langoustine soup or grilled langoustine tails

day_by_day.notes: This is another driving day covering approximately 200 km. Jökulsárlón is most magical at dusk when the icebergs glow. Boat tours on the lagoon are not available in January but the viewpoints are spectacular. Northern Lights reflecting on the lagoon is one of Iceland's most iconic sights – set an alarm for midnight if forecasts are good.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for sunrise at Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (around 11:00 AM in January) – the golden light on the icebergs is extraordinary. Spend the morning exploring both the main lagoon and Diamond Beach thoroughly. Look out for seals that often swim among the icebergs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive a short distance to meet your guide for the Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull. Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified mountain guide, then descend into a stunning natural ice cave with otherworldly blue ice formations. This is one of Iceland's most unique experiences only accessible in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the glacier tour (typically ends late afternoon). Drive back toward your accommodation near Höfn. Rest and recover from the physical glacier hike. Enjoy a hearty dinner and an early night – or if energy allows, watch for Northern Lights from outside the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast near Jökulsárlón
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by some glacier tour operators, or bring your own snacks and thermos – there are no restaurants near the glacier access points
meals.dinner: Cozy guesthouse dinner or return to Pakkhús in Höfn for a different dish – try the lamb fillet with Icelandic herbs

day_by_day.notes: Book the Vatnajökull glacier and ice cave tour well in advance – these tours are extremely popular and run in small groups for safety. Wear warm waterproof layers and sturdy boots (crampons provided). The tour is moderately physically demanding. Ice caves are only safely accessible November through March. Confirm tour meeting point when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the long but scenic drive back westward along the South Coast. Stop at the Foss á Síðu waterfall and enjoy the peaceful East Iceland landscapes. Drive through the Eldhraun lava fields again appreciating their alien beauty in the winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Skógar Folk Museum near Skógafoss for an afternoon visit – an excellent open-air museum showcasing traditional Icelandic turf houses and rural life through the centuries. Walk to Skógafoss waterfall for a second visit and attempt to climb the staircase beside it for elevated views if conditions are safe.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in the Selfoss or Hveragerði area and check into a mid-range guesthouse. Hveragerði is a geothermal town famous for its hot springs and greenhouses. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and explore the small town's geothermal park where hot water bubbles up through the ground.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Höfn area before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside café stop – try a bowl of lamb soup and fresh Icelandic bread at a local petrol station café (surprisingly good quality in Iceland)
meals.dinner: Varma Restaurant in Hveragerði or a local guesthouse dining room – try pan-fried trout with Icelandic vegetables grown in geothermal greenhouses

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day of approximately 250 km. Take breaks to stretch and enjoy viewpoints. Road conditions in January can be challenging – check road.is throughout the day. Hveragerði has a lovely geothermal river walk (Reykjadalur hot river) but it requires a 3 km hike each way – save this for tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to the Reykjadalur Hot River near Hveragerði – a 3 km trail each way leading to a natural geothermal river where you can bathe in warm flowing water surrounded by steaming hills. This is a hidden gem and one of Iceland's most unique hot spring experiences. The hike takes approximately 45 minutes each way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Reykjavík (approximately 45 minutes from Hveragerði). Check into a centrally located mid-range hotel in Reykjavík for the next few nights. Spend the afternoon exploring the Harpa Concert Hall and waterfront area, then visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) – an underground museum built around a 10th-century Viking longhouse.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's famous nightlife and restaurant scene on Laugavegur and Austurstræti streets. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant and sample Icelandic craft beers. If aurora activity is forecast, take a short drive outside the city after dinner for viewing.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Hveragerði – fuel up before the hike
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos and snacks for the Reykjadalur hike – there are no facilities on the trail. Grab lunch in Reykjavík after arrival at a downtown café
meals.dinner: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavík – famous for cast-iron pan fish dishes at mid-range prices; try the Arctic char or haddock pan

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike can be icy in January – wear crampons or hiking boots with good grip. Bring a change of clothes and swimwear for the river. The water temperature varies along the river – walk upstream for warmer spots. Leave valuables in the car as there are no lockers at the trailhead.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring more of Reykjavík's cultural highlights. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times. Then walk to the Sun Voyager sculpture on the waterfront – a beautiful Viking ship sculpture perfect for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum on Öskjuhlíð hill – a stunning glass-domed building with a real ice cave inside, Northern Lights planetarium show, and exhibits on Icelandic nature and geology. The 360-degree viewing deck offers panoramic views over Reykjavík and the surrounding mountains and ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Join a Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour departing from Reykjavík. The guide will monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive the group to the optimal location away from city light pollution. Hot chocolate is often provided. This is your dedicated aurora hunting evening with expert guidance.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavík
meals.lunch: Café at the National Museum or Perlan Museum café – try Icelandic meat soup or a skyr parfait
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro on Þórsgata – French-Icelandic fusion at mid-range prices; try the fish of the day or Icelandic lamb burger before the evening tour

day_by_day.notes: Book the Perlan Northern Lights show separately from the museum entrance. The Jeep aurora tour typically departs around 9–10 PM and returns by 1–2 AM. Tour operators have a flexible cancellation policy if cloud cover prevents viewing – they often reschedule for the next available night. Dress in your absolute warmest clothes for standing outside in January.

day_by_day.morning: Recover from the late aurora tour with a slow morning. After a late breakfast, visit the Reykjavík Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) or the Einar Jónsson Sculpture Museum for a dose of Icelandic art and culture. Browse the unique shops along Skólavörðustígur for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), design items, and gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day trip to the Reykjanes Peninsula – a dramatic volcanic landscape of lava fields, geothermal areas, and coastal cliffs. Visit the Bridge Between Continents where you can walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, the Gunnuhver hot spring area with its powerful mud pools and steam vents, and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík for a special farewell-style dinner at a nicer restaurant. Spend the evening packing and reflecting on the incredible experiences of the past 12 days. Do one final aurora check before bed – January nights in Iceland are long and the aurora can appear at any time.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – sleep in and enjoy a leisurely meal
meals.lunch: Local café near the Reykjanes Peninsula – try a fish and chips or lamb sandwich from a roadside café
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (The Fish Market) in Reykjavík – slightly splurge-worthy on the last full evening; try the sushi-style Icelandic fish tasting menu or the pan-seared cod with lobster bisque

day_by_day.notes: The Gunnuhver hot spring area on the Reykjanes Peninsula has been highly active geologically in recent years – check for any access restrictions or volcanic activity updates before visiting. Stay on marked paths at all times near geothermal features. The peninsula is approximately 45 minutes from Reykjavík city center.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final Icelandic breakfast at the hotel. Depending on your departure time, take one last walk along the Reykjavík waterfront or visit a local bakery for fresh pastries and coffee. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs at the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or shops along Laugavegur.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and drive to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 45–50 minutes from Reykjavík). Return your rental car if applicable. Allow extra time for icy road conditions in January. Clear security and enjoy the airport's duty-free Icelandic products – pick up Brennivín, Icelandic chocolate, or lopapeysa wool goods.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of Northern Lights, geothermal hot springs, glaciers, and the wild beauty of the Arctic island. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in one of the world's most magical destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – savor the skyr, smoked salmon, and Icelandic rye bread one last time
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavík – try a final bowl of lamb soup before departing
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your connection airport

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport is well-organized but can be busy. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. The airport has excellent duty-free shopping with genuine Icelandic products at competitive prices. If you have extra time before your flight, the airport is only 10 minutes from the Blue Lagoon – a perfect final soak if your flight departs in the evening (store luggage at the airport first).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind the lights while waiting for the show.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The naturally heated water sits at a perfect 37–39°C year-round. Includes access to steam caves, a lava sauna, and in-water silica mud mask treatments for a full rejuvenating experience.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling hot springs, and a small geyser. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this offers an authentic and intimate geothermal bathing experience in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Icelandic Food & Culture Walking Tour in Reykjavík
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavík's vibrant food scene on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup (kjötsúpa), fresh langoustine, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and the infamous hákarl (fermented shark). Visit local markets and learn about Viking-era culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified guide, then descend into a breathtaking natural ice cave glowing in shades of blue and crystal. Learn about Iceland's glacial geology and climate change impacts while experiencing one of the country's most dramatic landscapes up close.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort bar, and settle into your beachfront suite. If skies are clear, step outside for a spontaneous first glimpse of the Northern Lights from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and Icelandic craft beer or Brennivín schnapps arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pack warm layers in your carry-on for the airport transfer — January temperatures in Iceland regularly dip below -5°C. Confirm private transfer booking with resort concierge ahead of travel. Aurora alerts can be set up on your phone via the Icelandic Met Office app.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely luxury breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, meet with the resort concierge to review your full 13-day itinerary, arrange any outstanding bookings, and collect aurora forecast updates. Take a relaxed walk along the beachfront to acclimatize to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — one of Iceland's most iconic experiences. Soak in the milky-blue mineral-rich geothermal waters. Book the Premium or Retreat package for access to exclusive areas, an in-water floating massage, silica mud mask, and algae mask. Enjoy a glass of sparkling wine while soaking.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a fresh-up, then dine at the resort's signature restaurant. Toast to the start of an extraordinary Icelandic adventure.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast buffet at the Aegean Bliss Resort — skyr, smoked salmon, Icelandic rye bread, fresh pastries, and eggs
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — Michelin-quality Nordic cuisine with panoramic geothermal views; try the langoustine and Arctic char
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — multi-course tasting menu featuring Icelandic lamb, king crab, and seasonal root vegetables paired with Nordic wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa in advance as slots fill weeks ahead. January daylight hours are very limited (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30), so afternoon activities should begin by noon. Keep aurora app notifications on throughout the night.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Reykjavík beginning with Hallgrímskirkja Church for panoramic city views from the tower. Continue to the Harpa Concert Hall to admire its stunning geometric glass façade. Stroll the colorful streets of the old town at your leisure with your private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Icelandic Food & Culture Walking Tour in Reykjavík. Sample traditional Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb soup, kleinur pastries, and locally brewed craft beers. Explore hidden culinary gems and learn about Viking food heritage from your knowledgeable guide.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — depart from Reykjavík into the dark wilderness away from light pollution. Your expert guide will track aurora forecasts in real time and drive to optimal viewing locations. Hot chocolate and warm blankets provided in the jeep.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service at Aegean Bliss Resort — freshly squeezed juices, Icelandic pastries, smoked fish platter, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the food walking tour; supplement with a sit-down lunch at Dill Restaurant — Iceland's pioneering New Nordic fine dining establishment
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavík — inventive traditional Icelandic cuisine; try the cod head dish and slow-cooked lamb with wild herbs

day_by_day.notes: Dress in full thermal layers for the evening jeep tour — windchill in open terrain can be severe. The tour operator will advise on departure time based on that evening's aurora forecast (KP index). Photography tips for capturing the Northern Lights will be shared by your guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury day tour of the Golden Circle. Begin at Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley with a private guide and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area. Watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water up to 40 meters. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss Waterfall — one of Europe's most powerful waterfalls, partially frozen in January for a dramatic winter spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. Stop at Fontana Geothermal Baths in Laugarvatn for a private evening soak in natural geothermal pools on the shores of a volcanic lake. Enjoy the steam baths and, if conditions allow, a Northern Lights soak.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort breakfast — hot porridge with Icelandic bilberries, fresh bread, and local cheeses
meals.lunch: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn — intimate fine dining with locally sourced ingredients; known for Arctic char and Icelandic lamb
meals.dinner: Hotel Geysir Restaurant near Geysir — hearty Icelandic cuisine including slow-roasted lamb shank and wild mushroom soup in a cozy atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle roads may be icy in January — private vehicle with a 4WD and experienced driver is essential. Fontana evening visit should be pre-booked for a private session. Bring a waterproof bag for camera equipment near the waterfall.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the South Coast. Visit Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's most magical falls with a path leading behind the curtain of water (may be icy in January, guide will assess safety). Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall for dramatic rainbow-lit mist views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara near Vík. Marvel at the basalt column formations and the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks rising from the Atlantic. A private guide will explain the geological history and local folklore. Visit the picturesque village of Vík.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at a luxury boutique guesthouse near Vík or continue to a pre-arranged premium accommodation for the night. Enjoy a quiet evening with aurora watching from the countryside — the South Coast offers excellent dark sky conditions.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by Aegean Bliss Resort — thermos of coffee, artisan sandwiches, fruit, and Icelandic yogurt
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík — panoramic ocean views with fresh fish soup, lobster bisque, and lamb burgers
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — cozy fine dining with Icelandic lamb, pan-fried Arctic char, and homemade skyr desserts

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach carries a serious sneaker wave risk — never turn your back on the ocean and always heed your guide's instructions. January ice may close the path behind Seljalandsfoss; guide will confirm on the day. Overnight stay near Vík recommended to reduce driving time for Day 6.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Vatnajökull National Park for the Glacier Hike & Ice Cave Exploration on Vatnajökull. Meet your certified glacier guides and gear up with crampons, helmets, and harnesses. Hike across the vast ice fields of Europe's largest glacier with dramatic crevasse formations all around.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into a breathtaking natural ice cave beneath the glacier. Marvel at the electric blue ice formations sculpted by centuries of glacial movement. Your guide will explain glaciology and the impact of climate change on Iceland's ice caps. Photography time in the cave included.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward the resort or overnight luxury accommodation in the Jökulsárlón area. Visit Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon at twilight — floating blue icebergs calved from the glacier drift silently toward the sea, often illuminated by the Northern Lights overhead.

meals.breakfast: Hearty hot breakfast at overnight accommodation — eggs, Icelandic sausages, and fresh bread to fuel the glacier day
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch provided by glacier tour operator — insulated containers with hot soup, sandwiches, and energy bars consumed on the glacier
meals.dinner: Jökulsárlón area restaurant or Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon — fresh catch of the day, Icelandic lamb stew, and homemade desserts

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours are weather and safety dependent — your guide makes the final call on the day. Wear moisture-wicking base layers under glacier gear. Crampons and all safety equipment are provided. Keep camera batteries warm in an inner pocket as cold drains them rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort via the scenic Ring Road. Stop at the Diamond Beach adjacent to Jökulsárlón to photograph crystal-clear ice chunks washed ashore on the black sand — a surreal and otherworldly scene unique to Iceland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at the resort. Enjoy a full afternoon of relaxation — use the resort's spa facilities, heated infinity pool, and sauna. Book an in-resort massage or thermal body treatment to recover from the glacier adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Second Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a dedicated evening excursion into the wilderness for another aurora-chasing opportunity. January's long dark nights maximize viewing windows. Hot drinks and light snacks provided.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at overnight accommodation — light and energizing before the drive
meals.lunch: Roadside gourmet stop — Skaftá Bistro or similar en route; lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining — seven-course Nordic tasting menu with wine pairing; sommelier-curated Icelandic and Scandinavian wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 5–6 hours for the return drive from Jökulsárlón to the resort area. Road conditions on the Ring Road in January can be challenging — private 4WD with experienced driver is essential. Rest well before the evening jeep tour.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter tour over the Reykjanes Peninsula and volcanic landscapes (arrange through resort concierge with a luxury aviation provider). Aerial views of geothermal fields, lava flows, and the dramatic coastline are extraordinary in winter light. Land near a remote geothermal area for a private guided walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating back to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated spring water surrounded by steaming geothermal vents and open Icelandic countryside. Far more intimate than the Blue Lagoon with an authentic local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a private chef's dinner experience — arrange with resort concierge for an exclusive in-suite or private dining room dinner featuring a bespoke Icelandic menu prepared by the head chef.

meals.breakfast: Resort in-room breakfast — continental spread with fresh pastries, smoked salmon, and pressed juices delivered to your suite
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet box at the Secret Lagoon area — artisan cheeses, cured meats, Icelandic flatbread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner — five-course bespoke menu with lobster, Icelandic lamb, and seasonal foraged ingredients paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours require advance booking and are subject to weather and visibility conditions — have a backup activity planned. The Secret Lagoon is more relaxed and less crowded than Blue Lagoon, ideal for a mid-trip wind-down. Evening private dining should be arranged at least 48 hours in advance with the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Snowmobile adventure on Langjökull Glacier — Iceland's second largest glacier. A luxury private transfer takes you to the glacier where you board powerful snowmobiles and race across the vast white plateau with a certified guide. Optionally enter the man-made ice tunnel inside the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hraunfossar and Barnafoss Waterfalls in West Iceland — two of Iceland's most unique waterfalls where water seeps through ancient lava fields in hundreds of tiny streams. Stunning in winter with ice formations framing the cascades.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the West Iceland region before returning to the resort. Aurora watch on the return drive — the open landscapes of West Iceland provide excellent dark sky conditions.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at resort — Icelandic oatmeal with bilberries, eggs, and strong coffee before an active day
meals.lunch: Húsafell Resort Restaurant — locally sourced Icelandic cuisine in a stunning wilderness setting near the glacier
meals.dinner: Settlement Center Restaurant in Borgarnes — Viking-inspired Icelandic cuisine; try the lamb and fish dishes with local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobiling requires a valid driving license. Full safety briefing and gear (helmet, suit, gloves) provided. Langjökull is at altitude — dress in maximum thermal layers. Confirm snowmobile booking through resort concierge well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full spa and wellness morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Indulge in a geothermal body wrap, hot stone massage, and facial using Icelandic volcanic mineral products. Use the resort's private thermal pools and steam rooms at leisure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private photography workshop with a professional Icelandic landscape photographer. Head to scenic coastal or lava field locations near the resort to capture Iceland's unique winter light, dramatic skies, and black sand coastlines. Perfect for improving your Northern Lights photography technique ahead of the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Third Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — your most experienced jeep aurora excursion yet, with aurora forecasting knowledge accumulated over the trip. Your guide will take you to a new location for fresh perspectives on the phenomenon.

meals.breakfast: Slow, indulgent resort breakfast — eggs benedict with smoked salmon, fresh juice bar, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Resort poolside or lounge lunch — light Nordic salads, open-faced smørrebrød sandwiches, and seafood chowder
meals.dinner: Pre-tour early dinner at resort — warming lamb stew, dark rye bread, and Icelandic dairy desserts before the evening jeep departure

day_by_day.notes: This is a dedicated recovery and enrichment day — pace yourself after the high-activity days. The photography workshop doubles as preparation for the evening aurora hunt. Bring all camera equipment fully charged and with spare batteries.

day_by_day.morning: Whale watching and puffin boat tour from Reykjavík Old Harbour (winter whale watching season — humpbacks and minke whales are commonly spotted). Board a luxury yacht or premium vessel with heated indoor viewing areas and expert marine biologists on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula — visit the Bridge Between Continents (walk between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), Gunnuhver geothermal hot springs, and the dramatic coastal cliffs at Reykjanesviti lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-penultimate dinner at one of Reykjavík's finest restaurants. Celebrate the journey with a blow-out luxury dining experience featuring Iceland's finest ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — light and energizing before the boat departure
meals.lunch: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavík — upscale Icelandic grill restaurant with dry-aged lamb, langoustine, and volcanic stone-cooked meats
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's most exclusive dining experience; a 20-seat counter restaurant with a theatrical tasting menu; advance booking essential

day_by_day.notes: Winter whale watching success rates are high in Iceland — humpback whales are frequently spotted in Faxaflói Bay. Dress in full thermals for the boat even with indoor heating. Óx Restaurant requires booking weeks or months in advance — arrange through resort concierge immediately upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long breakfast, pack souvenirs, and take a final beachfront walk. Visit the resort boutique for premium Icelandic gifts — woolen lopapeysa sweaters, volcanic sea salt, and Icelandic skincare products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final hot spring experience — return to the Blue Lagoon for a relaxed afternoon soak, this time using the Retreat Spa's most exclusive facilities. Enjoy floating in the warm geothermal waters as a perfect final Iceland memory.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a private farewell dinner. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days in Iceland over a curated multi-course meal with wine pairing. Northern Lights watch from the resort terrace as a final send-off from the Icelandic sky.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at resort — the full spread of Icelandic specialties enjoyed at a leisurely pace
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — a fitting bookend to the trip; enjoy the same stunning geothermal views as Day 2
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — chef's special farewell tasting menu with Icelandic champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing and organizing luggage this evening. Confirm departure transfer timing with resort concierge. Check aurora forecast for a final potential sighting from the resort — January nights offer maximum darkness for viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a last Icelandic breakfast, check out, and arrange private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Allow extra time for winter road conditions and airport security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Browse the duty-free for final Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Icelandic schnapps), chocolate, and beauty products. Reflect on an unforgettable 13-day premium Icelandic adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Settle in with memories of Northern Lights, glacier ice caves, geothermal lagoons, and Iceland's extraordinary volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — skyr parfait, Icelandic rye bread with smoked salmon, and a perfect last coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a final Icelandic meal at Keflavík Airport restaurant — fish and chips or lamb burger
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the airport transfer, check-in, and security in January due to potential weather delays.
